name: ctdose-core-ge-validation-arm
reason: Unresolved AI finding; inspect evidence, not majority vote

tests.framework: standard unittest, in the frozen snapshot under python -I

not_covered_by_this_framework: The project's real suite is pytest (449 tests) and AI-Check v1 accepts only `unittest discover`. It was run separately and passed; that is reported as a separate check and is NOT part of this PASS/FAIL.
The GE sample objects themselves (OpenREM/PixelMed, GPL-3.0) were not sent; only measurements derived from them. Re-parsing them is a local check.
No figure, PDF page or built document was reviewed here.
unresolved: FAIL. Both reviewers independently found that NO_TABLE_FEED_TYPES conflates axial step-and-shoot with stationary dwell. VCT event 12 is a sequenced acquisition over 397.5 mm with pitch 1.0: the table does move, so the stated exclusion reason does not apply to it. Events 23-26 (pitch 0.1, length 0.0) are correctly excluded but for a different reason.

The headline's '+11.6 %, all four within 20 %' rests on an arbitrary tie-break. For the Optima 660 at the 32 cm phantom the conventional 'medium' filter is not tabulated and _nearest_bowtie breaks the tie between 'small' and 'large' by list order, choosing 'small' for a body phantom. With the 'large' body filter the two Optima errors become +21.3 % and +22.4 %, the median +18.9 %, and two of four fall outside 20 %. Verified locally after the review.

Claude: the arm argues the recorded 2.5/5.0 mm is not a beam width, then uses the row nearest to that same figure, and the note says the headline 'uses the collimation the RDSR records', which is false -- 10 mm is not recorded.

Both: the duration ratio is algebraically 40/recorded collimation and so has no empirical content; DCM 113824 exposure time, or DLP/CTDIvol for the irradiated length, would test the premise directly and neither is used.
Both: test_ge_arm_recompute.py reads only the output file, so it shares every upstream decision and its claim to re-derive 'every reported number' is overstated.
